data.name: Spirits: Ciel Bleu
data.detailed_description:
Story

Willard Rouse is an ordinary 17-year high school student who is often by himself. By accident, he discovered that he is a spirit bearer, one who could summon and use the power of spirits. After getting kicked out of Rainvalley Academy, he transferred to Ficaso Academy. Much to his surprise, Willard found himself in the company of great friends at Ficaso which led him to think that he could finally enjoy his years in high school without being misunderstood. However, Ficaso Academy is not what it appears to be. Willard started to have suspicions when he learned that the school prohibits students to make contact with the outside world until they graduate. Eventually, Willard realized that all the students in Ficaso are spirit bearers but they are unable to summon their spirits due to spirit jammers strategically placed around the academy. What secrets lie beneath the walls of Ficaso Academy? What challenges await Willard and his friends in their quest to escape?

Discover the secrets of Ficaso Academy; learn more about Shades, creatures who devour the souls of spirit bearers, and meet the powerful Spirits that could be summoned by Willard and his friends. Watch Willard hone his spirit powers and develop his relationships with the people around him!

reviews.review:
[i] Spirits: Ciel Bleu [/i] is a short (about 3 hours) kinetic visual novel. Actually, there's one choice but not that meaningful. 

It's really sad but I'm afraid I can't recommend this visual novel. Again that dilemma between pretty art and poor writing. I really loved visuals here: bright and soothing anime-like style, though far from perfect, for example, sometimes a bit disproportional. The backgrounds are especially cute, in my opinion. It would be nice to have a CG gallery. And also, maybe it's not the best idea to use a CG from the 'final boss battle' for the game cover, kinda spoilerish xD 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1721113011 
As for the novel part, first what caught my attention was way too many typos and mistakes for such a short game. I even checked several times if the dev is a native speaker because that amount of mistakes I usually see in visual novels made by my native Russian developers. *Sigh* The game needs some serious editing. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1721034664 
Writing is kinda simple to my taste and the plot is a bit predictable with some issues, at least for me personally. Though I liked the idea of spirit bearers. The story seems quite dynamic, lots of changes, nothing to be bored about. But to the point when the whole story is a tad rushed, no depth at all, some details would be nice. It feels more like a generic retelling. For example, I got really interested when MC was brought to the spirit realm and his training started. But we got just zero details of what he was doing. Yeah, growing more muscles was mentioned but is it really the most important thing for a SPIRIT bearer?! Well, ok, who am I to even doubt, not an expert in this sphere for sure, I guess it matters but what about other more spirit-related things? Nothing. I'm utterly disappointed. I liked the idea so much but it wasn't implemented at all. If only the story were longer and more detailed. One of the reviewers mentioned that the game stirs imagination, yeah, right, because you actually HAVE TO imagine lots of stuff to propel the plot. That's not how the storytelling should work. I get it that some details can be omitted but not all the time. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1721113040 
The final scenes were actually rather sweet, swaying my general impression to the more positive side. So I can't say it was a complete disaster. Nope, I enjoyed bright visuals, and the main idea but it turned out to be quite a superficial game, unfortunately.

reviews.developer_response: We appreciate your review and understand your concerns. This VN was the first attempt of a newest developer and sadly this version of the game was all he had left after his main hdd failed, so we was unable to edit the game into a better state and decided to release it instead of scrapping all his hard work. Again, thank you for the feedback and I'll make sure this developers next title wont have the same mistakes in it :)
